name: the Miramare park
title: Ancient Trees in the Miramare Park, Trieste: 12 to Find
meta_description: A Habsburg archduke planted this park on bare rock in 1856 to see what would survive. Twelve of the trees did, from California and the Mediterranean.
intro:
The man who planted these trees was shot by a firing squad in Mexico eleven years later. Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg began the Miramare park in the spring of 1856 on a limestone headland with almost no soil on it, and he ran the whole thing as an experiment: he wanted to know which foreign species would hold on to bare Adriatic rock. The soil was carted in.

The answer is still standing. Twelve of the trees we map grow here. A third of them are Californian: two coast redwoods over four metres round, a Monterey cypress of the same girth, and a ghost pine whose needles sit so thinly on the branch that you can see the sky through its crown. Six Aleppo pines, all individually registered as monumental, share the grounds with a holm oak whose 5.2 metre trunk two official surveys cannot agree is one stem or three. The park is free and open daily. Only the castle charges admission.
